:::{#thm-mutual-information-self}
#### Mutual information of a variable with itself

For a [discrete random variable](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-discrete-rv) $X$
with finite entropy, <!-- check-term-links: allow -->

$$I(X; X) = H(X).$$

:::

::: {.proof}

Given $X=x$, the variable $X$ equals $x$ with probability $1$,
so $p(x \mid x) = 1$ and $p(x' \mid x) = 0$ for every $x' \ne x$.
Only the term with $x' = x$ contributes to the entropy of $X$ given $X=x$,
and it is $-1 \cdot \log 1 = 0$:

$$H(X \mid X=x) = 0.$$

Averaging over the distribution of $X$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
H(X \mid X)
&= \sum_{x} p(x) \, H(X \mid X=x) \\
&= 0.
\end{aligned}
$$

By @def-mutual-information with $Y = X$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
I(X; X)
&= H(X) - H(X \mid X) \\
&= H(X).
\end{aligned}
$$

:::
